description:
Server logs are a way to keep a record of what happens in your server. When something happens, such as a member joining or a message being deleted, Wynem will send a log message to a channel of your choice.

Each log type has its own channel setting, so you can send different types of logs to different channels, or send them all to the same channel. Every log includes a timestamp of when it was sent.

Logs are delivered using a webhook named **Wynem - Server logs**, so Wynem requires the `Manage Webhooks` permission to send them. Managing and viewing the logs requires the `Manage Guild` permission. If Wynem ever loses access to a logs channel or its webhook, that log type is automatically removed.
Here is an example of the `member-join` log:
There are `23` different log types, and each one can be sent to its own channel:

rows: When a member joins the server
When a member leaves the server
When a member sets, changes, or removes a nickname
When a member gains or loses a role
When a member sets, changes, or removes a server avatar
When member joins, switches, or leaves a voice channel
When a ghost ping is detected
When a reaction is added to a message for the first time
When a moderator uses the addnote command
When a blocked emoji reaction gets removed
When a moderator uses the endtimeout command
When a moderator uses the purge command
When a moderator uses the timeout command
When a moderator uses the warn command
When a member that is new to Discord joins the server
When a server invite is created
When a server invite is deleted

tabs.name: Setting up logs
content: To set up the server logs, use the <command:managelogs|serverconfig logs manage> command to open the log manager. Use the select menu to choose the log type you want to set up.

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!managelogsused /serverconfig logs manage

content: After selecting a log type, the manager will show the channel currently set for that type. A channel select menu will appear, along with a select menu to change the log type you are editing. Choose the channel you want the logs sent to, then press the `Set logs channel` button.

content: The manager stays open after setting a channel, so you can select another log type and continue setting up more logs. After a while of inactivity, the manager will time out.

tabs.name: Viewing the logs
content: To view the currently set up log channels, use the <command:viewlogs|serverconfig logs view> command.

reply.name: Ewan
reply.message: e!viewlogsused /serverconfig logs view

content: If there are no logs set up in the server, you will be told so instead.

data.title: No server logs
data.description: There are no server logs set up in this server

tabs.name: Removing logs
content: To remove a log, open the log manager with the <command:managelogs|serverconfig logs manage> command and select the log type you want to remove. Leave the channel select menu empty, then press the `Set logs channel` button.
